findings.title: Verification walkthrough invokes a bench entry point and flags that do not exist
findings.description: All five walkthrough steps use `python scripts/bench.py --backend ... --config ... --ticks ... --parity-check ... --subdivision-factor ...`. The repository has no `scripts/bench.py` (only `scripts/148_*.py` measurement scripts), and the real harness CLI (`src/migratory/bench/cli.py`) is `python -m migratory.bench --workload <name> --backend <name>` with only `--workload`, `--backend`, `--workload-dir`, `--results-dir`, `--list-*` flags — no `--config`, `--ticks`, `--N`, `--parity-check`, or `--subdivision-factor`. Every gate (A1–A5) is verified through this walkthrough, so as written it cannot be executed. Compounding this, Intervention 2 says S is added "to the bench configuration" but never says *where*: a new CLI flag (as the walkthrough implies), a workload YAML field (where `max_neighbors=32` already lives in `src/migratory/bench/workload.py`), or a `BenchConfig`/`GpuAgentState` field (where `cell_size` is currently derived at `quadrants_fused_state.py:150`). The walkthrough also uses `pytest` where project convention is `uv run pytest`. The doc's own note ("draft demo script; will be refined") softens but does not resolve this — the design should specify the flag/config surface it is adding, since that is part of the slice's deliverable.

findings.title: Gate ablation compares two identical commands; no mechanism specified to toggle counter-gating vs. early exit
findings.description: Step 3 defines four ablation runs: "Baseline (S=1, counter-gating)", "Early exit only (S=1, break enabled)", "Cell subdivision only (S=3, counter-gating)", "Both (S=3, break enabled)". The first two commands are byte-for-byte identical (`--subdivision-factor 1 --ticks 200`), and S=3's "counter-gating" variant likewise has no distinguishing flag. The design specifies only an `S` knob; it specifies no way to disable the `break` and run the slice-145 counter-gating path for comparison. Without one, the "baseline" and "early-exit only" rows of the ablation cannot be produced as described, and A2's "≥5× faster than slice 145 CUDA baseline" loses its in-run control (it can fall back to the recorded 38 TPS from slice 145, but the walkthrough explicitly promises a reproduced baseline: "should reproduce slice 145 ~38 TPS"). Either add a spec'd toggle (e.g. `S=0`-style sentinel is *not* acceptable per the no-silent-placeholder rule — an explicit config flag is) or rewrite the walkthrough to compare against the recorded slice 145 numbers.

findings.title: A5's primary verification method is documented as unavailable on the CUDA host
findings.description: A5 says register spill is "confirmed via `nvcc --ptxas-info` or benchmark log", and Step 4 (lines 180-182) directs the reader to look for `lmem` when `TI_PRINT_KERNEL_STATS=1 or equivalent`. Slice 148's envelope measurement (project-documents/user/notes/148-notes.envelope-measurement.md, §2A) explicitly records that "`ptxas`, `cuobjdump`, and `nvcc` are not installed on this host — only the CUDA runtime driver," and that slice obtained the same register/spill evidence by inspecting the Quadrants PTX cache (`~/.cache/quadrants/qdcache/...ptx`, `.local` declarations = 0) plus `qd.profiler`. The design's fallback is hedged ("or equivalent", `TI_PRINT_KERNEL_STATS` is a Taichi variable, unverified for Quadrants 0.7.5) — the exact anti-pattern the re-diagnosis notes for this very slice warn against ("when debugging, get the actual error message" / no speculative mechanisms). Since A5 is a gate, the walkthrough should name the method proven to work on this host (PTX cache inspection / `qd.profiler.print_kernel_profiler_info()`), with the nvcc path as secondary.

findings.title: Plan entry's 7-neighbor benchmark target is dropped from the design
findings.description: The slice plan entry (project-documents/user/architecture/140-slices.simulation-scaling.md:50) states: "the 7-neighbor operating point is a benchmark target," echoing the re-diagnosis notes' observation that at `max_neighbors=7` the counter-gating waste is worst and early-exit gain scales with `candidates/max_neighbors`. The design's only benchmark configuration is fixed at `max_neighbors=32` (line 128, and no gate run varies it). Either carry the `max_neighbors=7` run into the gate set (it is cheap — one more bench invocation on the same host) or state explicitly why it is deferred, so the plan entry and the design don't diverge silently.

findings.title: `break` exits only the innermost per-cell loop; remaining cells in the scan block are still entered
findings.description: The proposed `break` is inside `for kk in range(start, end)`, so once the cap is hit, the agent still enters the remaining `drow`/`dcol` cell iterations of the 3×3 (or 7×7 at S=3) block — each doing a first-iteration break check. The residual cost is bounded by (2S+1)² ≈ 48 loop entries per capped agent, which is negligible against the ~45,000 candidates removed, so this is not a defect; but the design's "early exit" framing implies the whole scan terminates. One sentence acknowledging the bounded per-cell re-entry cost (or hoisting the cap test to the cell-loop level if Quadrants permits a nested break) would close the gap between the stated mechanism and the implemented one.

findings.title: Subdivision formula should reference `max_query_radius`, not per-profile `query_radius`
findings.description: The design states `cell_size = query_radius / S`, but the code derives `cell_size = max_query_radius * DEFAULT_CELL_SIZE_MULTIPLIER` (`quadrants_fused_state.py:150,151`) precisely so a single cell size covers *every* profile's query radius — the invariant that makes the (2S+1) cell walk sufficient. Writing the formula with the max (and noting S replaces/parameterizes `DEFAULT_CELL_SIZE_MULTIPLIER`) keeps the single-source-of-truth property and prevents a mixed-profile workload from under-covering the largest-radius profile. Also, the Component Interactions diagram's `build_spatial_hash(cell_size=cell_size)` misstates the signature — it takes `state` and reads `state.cell_size` (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:411`); the prose immediately below ("only the cell_size value changes") is correct.
